correctness.rationale: PASS: A generic central section vertex corresponds one-to-one to a crossed 4-cube edge, with crossing criterion abs(sum remaining signed coordinates)<u_i. After sorting four positive normal coordinates a<b<c<d, the two possible signed-sum changes X=d-a-b-c and Y=d+a-b-c partition the parameter cone into three types with facet inventories 4^6, 3^2 5^6, 4^6 6^2. Independently re-enumerated exact cube-edge crossings at (1,2,3,7),(1,2,3,5),(6,8,10,11), giving 8,12,12 vertices and the stated facets. A prescribed edge has crossing probability P(|N(0,1)|>sqrt3 |N(0,1)|)=1/3, so expected count 32/3 and dominant type probability 1/3. Reflection T(u)=u-(Y/2)(1,-1,-1,1) is orthogonal, involutive, and preserves the ordered non-dominant cone while swapping the remaining two types; Gaussian radial density is invariant, forcing their conditional 1:1 split. Boundary hyperplanes have Haar probability zero. Exact geometry, not simulation, proves the masses.
